problem: LLM-based VLN agents (Uni-NaVid, StreamVLN, InternVLA-N1) depend on dense step-by-step instructions and are trained with short-horizon action supervision (4-8 steps). This makes them short-sighted in beyond-the-view navigation (BVN), producing unexpected turning and dead-end trapping. Extending the supervision horizon destabilizes LLM training.
motivation: Real-world navigation should work from simple high-level intents, so agents must find distant unseen targets without granular guidance. Video generation models are pre-trained to capture long-horizon futures aligned with language, so they are a natural source of long-horizon foresight. Continuous video generation is too slow and redundant, so the paper uses sparse future frames to extend the horizon and cut cost.
key_idea: Use a video generation model to imagine a sparse 20-second future (fixed-interval frames) and condition an inverse-dynamics action head on it, with distillation and history compression to reach sub-second real-time inference.
insight: Long-horizon foresight is what matters for BVN. Ablation (a), with a 2-chunk continuous horizon that emulates short-sighted LLMs, gets only 2.5% BVN, versus 11.7% for a 10-chunk continuous horizon and 25.0% for the sparse 20 s model. Sparsification gives the long horizon at lower cost (1.7x inference speed-up, 1.4x training speed-up) with a moderate loss compared with the dense 20-chunk oracle (35.8%). Distillation gives about 10x speed-up, and the Former history compression keeps latency flat as history grows.
method: Sparse video supervision: predict frames at T+1, T+2, T+5, T+8, ..., T+20 (interval 3 after two continuous chunks), covering 20 s at 4 FPS
Data curation: 140 h of stabilized handheld DJI Osmo Action 4 video, about 13k trajectories, with actions labeled by Depth Anything 3 pose estimation and manual language annotation
Stage 1: adapt Wan2.1-1.3B T2V to I2V with a flow-matching loss on sparse chunk latents
Stage 2: history injection through added zero-initialized cross-attention blocks, with history compressed by Q-Former (temporal) and Video-Former (spatial), CDiT-inspired
Stage 3: PCM-style diffusion distillation adapted to flow matching, from 50 to 4 denoising steps with 4 phases

Stage 4: freeze the distilled VGM and train a DiT action head (23.4M parameters, inverse dynamics, DDIM) via cross-attention on the generated sparse future and the language, using DA3-relabeled actions on generated frames; predicts 8-step continuous actions
Deployment: remote RTX 4090 server with sub-second inference, driving a Unitree Go2 robot dog

setting.backbone: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B video generation model (fine-tuned, distilled to 4 steps) + Q-Former/Video-Former + DiT action head
setting.model_size: 1.3B Wan backbone (1.8B with history modules), 23.4M action head
setting.training_data: 140 h of self-collected real-world handheld navigation videos (~13k trajectories, 4 FPS), with DA3-derived actions and manual language annotations; no simulation data
setting.observation: monocular RGB (upward-facing stabilized DJI Osmo Action 4) with history of past frames
setting.action_space: continuous relative motion (Δx, Δy, Δθ), 8-step trajectories

numbers.eval_set_note: 6 unseen real-world scenes, 4 tasks each (2 IFN + 2 BVN), 10 trials per task, 240 trials per model
numbers.backbone: Wan2.1-1.3B, distilled 4 steps, 20 s sparse horizon
numbers.extra: success = stop within 1.5 m of target; real-world zero-shot; success rate reported separately for IFN and BVN tasks
numbers.evidence: Table 1, Total column: SparseVideoNav IFN 50.0, BVN 25.0

numbers.extra: no distillation, dense continuous generation; slower inference

numbers_note: Only real-world success rates are reported, on a custom benchmark; no standard benchmarks. Latency and FVD results appear only in figures. The 17.5% night-scene BVN figure in the text is the mean of Square 20 and Mountain 15.
results: On real-world zero-shot evaluation, SparseVideoNav reaches 50.0% IFN and 25.0% BVN average success, versus the strongest baseline StreamVLN at 35.0% and 10.0% (+15.0 each), giving about 2.5x the BVN success rate. It is the only method with non-zero BVN success at night (Square 20, Mountain 15). It also gives a 27x speed-up over the unoptimized counterpart with sub-second inference.
limitations: Only 140 h of data, far below web scale; mode collapse occurs in highly challenging scenarios
Inference is still slightly slower than LLM-based paradigms such as StreamVLN
Evaluation is small-scale (240 trials) and uses a custom real-world benchmark with a proximity-only success criterion
